ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $3.33 to the rider for the unexcused off-route segment (RD-2); no account flag (RD-6 not met).
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is RydeTAXI, so the fare is meter-based and detour km feed directly into the fare [F4][F7][RD-2][RD-1]. One off-route segment is on record: 21:57–22:04, 4.13 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.77 km, +2.36 km [F3].

No exemption applies. The rider-requested-stop branch fails: there is no rider message naming any place, and in fact no in-app chat at all [F8][RD-3]. The consent branch fails: the only source of an alleged agreement is the driver's post-trip statement, which is a claim, not rider consent, and it is written after the segment [F9][RD-5][G11]. The reasonable-cause branch fails: the only traffic item is an accident reported 22:07 along the optimal route, later than the segment's 21:57 start, and the speed bands on AYE and CTE are band 4 (30–39 km/h), which at most corroborates and cannot exempt on its own [F3][F4][F10][F11][F12][RD-4].

Amount: the segment's extra 2.36 km × this trip's per-km rate = $26.93 ÷ 19.10 km = $1.4099/km; 2.36 km × $1.4099/km = $3.3274 → $3.33 [F4][F7][RD-2][RD-1]. The billed excess of $3.62 covers 2.57 km, which includes residual corridor/matching km that RD-2 does not refund, so only the segment's own extra km are refunded [F4].

RD-6 does not apply: the driver profile shows 4 disputes but 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days, so this is not a repeated breach and no account flag is warranted [F15][RD-6]. The rider's profile facts are not used to decide anything [F14].
